## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs to lower-case the key before storing it. Right now any value set under a mixed-case key can't be read back, which breaks the method this pull request adds.

## Changes
The pull request adds `Cache.set(key, value)`, which stores a value with an expiry of `time.monotonic() + ttl`. It also raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 and updates the comment to match. New tests cover the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` stores under `"Alpha"` while `get` (line 17) looks up `key.lower()`. This breaks the rule at app/cache.py:14-15: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together." — Values set with any uppercase letter can never be read back, and they never expire out of `_store` because `get` only deletes the lower-cased key. — Fix: Use `self._store[key.lower()] = ...` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` so it calls `set` with a mixed-case key; the test currently only sets `"alpha"`, so it cannot catch this.
